how_to_score: Loaded first by every flow on the platform, so its effect is the FLOOR under every other skill: the rules that hold whether or not the flow's own skill restates them. Scored from zz.event across runs — which refusals recur under it, and whether they are ones it already answers.

dimensions.name: Refusals it already answers do not recur
dimensions.evidence: Refusal classes stamped to runs that loaded zz-backbone, against the rules it states.
dimensions.five: The refusals this skill exists to prevent — an ungated write, a path shape it defines, an approval named wrongly — do not appear in runs that loaded it. Where one does, its text is what tells the agent how to recover, and the run recovers without asking.
dimensions.one: The same refusal class recurs in run after run that loaded this skill, because the rule is stated somewhere the reader does not reach it, or is stated as prose where the failure is mechanical. ops-intent teaching approve("<initiative>/intent.md") and an agent sending that literal placeholder is the shape of this failure.

dimensions.name: One statement of a platform rule
dimensions.evidence: Whether a flow's own skills restate what this one already says, and whether the two agree.
dimensions.five: Gates, document paths, credentials, block choice and sources are stated here and nowhere else. A flow's skills refer to the rule rather than repeating it, so there is one place to change it and no way for two places to disagree.
dimensions.one: Flow skills carry their own copies of platform rules. They drift, and a reader following one is refused by a platform enforcing the other — with nothing in either text to say which is current.

dimensions.name: Flow-agnostic in fact, not only in claim
dimensions.evidence: Whether its text turns out to be usable by sdlc-flow and casebox-assist, not only ops-flow.
dimensions.five: Nothing here assumes ops-flow's six stages, its document names, or its gate count. A new flow can load it first and get real value without editing it.
dimensions.one: It is ops-flow's rules with a platform label. Another flow loading it first is told things that do not apply to it, which teaches its agents to skim the spine — the one skill that most needs reading.
